findings: The registry names Utrecht BA Taalwetenschap, ISAT 56803, with Dutch language registration. The degree provides Dutch and English tracks. This example uses the Dutch track, whose governing regulations describe English lectures apart from the all-Dutch Language and Society specialization, Dutch seminar groups in the core where possible, and Dutch assessments as an available option. The selected Language and Cognition specialization best matches the generic degree’s defining questions about structure, acquisition and processing. The OER requires a 120 EC major comprising two 30 EC introductory packages, 15 EC of mandatory methods, a 30 EC specialization, 7.5 EC thesis preparation and 7.5 EC thesis. Annex 3 requires a coherent package within the 60 EC profiling space. The 30 EC package can be a minor, an additional specialization or approved study abroad. The other 30 EC remain electives under the degree rules. The mandatory basic grammar test is zero-credit.

Year 1 uses four periods with two 7.5 EC courses in each, beginning with Introduction and Psychology of Language, then Meaning and Comparative Morphosyntax, then Sociolinguistics and Digital Tools, then Language Development and Phonetics. The catalog shows C/AD, C/AD, AB/C and AD/C respectively. In year two Methods and Statistics takes period 1 C alongside Experimental Psycholinguistics B. Phonology and Fieldwork takes period 3 AC alongside Semantics and Pragmatics D. The Grammar of Words is in period 2 and Language Acquisition and Language Structure in period 4. The two open places in periods 2 and 4 give 15 EC of other electives. In year three Capstone is placed in period 1 and thesis in period 2. The capstone prior-knowledge field requires three specialization courses, and the thesis requires that most of the major be completed. The example completes all four specialization courses and 105 EC of the major before the capstone, and 112.5 EC before the thesis. Both methods courses, all four specialization courses and both research elements are at level 3, yielding 60 advanced EC above the 45 EC minimum. The remaining 45 EC of profiling can include the coherent package and 15 EC of other electives, completing 60 EC in each year. The future sequence illustrates the entrant cohort using current period patterns.

The closest plan joins Psycholinguistics, neurobiology, perception and higher cognition with stylistics, rhetoric, philosophical theories of mind, empirical statistics and synthesis of research. Lifespan Developmental Psychology supplies developmental context, while child language acquisition is specifically evidenced in Psycholinguistics. The description-only perception and psycholinguistics courses supply meaningful direct or enabling content. The society option replaces peripheral archaeology and art selections with a sequence in sociology, community rhetoric, brain and behavior and Psycholinguistics. Stylistics and discourse, multilingual cognition, community speaking, qualitative research, social theory and media representation give complementary language and society perspectives. It offers qualitative field methods for social questions rather than phonological fieldwork. The computational plan combines Python, logic, probability, linear algebra and data methods with machine learning, neural language models, stylistics and psycholinguistics. Computer vision contributes transferable pattern recognition; general AI decision and optimization courses do not count as language modelling on their own. The computational option covers selected elements of language computation, with no dedicated corpus-linguistics sequence. The three options exceed the pairwise four-course threshold. Four bounded pairings cover meaning, methods, language processing and digital data. Dedicated grammar, speech sounds and fieldwork remain visible as distinct external subjects. The required Utrecht thesis and the optional 15 EC UCR comparison element are separately identified.
